title: Diver Finds 162-Year-Old Guinness That May Be Drinkable
paragraphs: Divers exploring a shipwreck off the coast of England have found bottles of Guinness that are about 162 years old, and they believe the beer inside may still be drinkable.

The bottles were found in the wreck of a sailing ship that sank about 5 kilometers off the coast of Dover. The ship had left London for Vancouver, in Canada, in November 1864. A week later, on November 27, it collided with another ship and sank. The ship was called the Mindoro.

The discovery was made by Stefan Panis, an expedition diver. While exploring the ship's cargo hold, he found a sealed bottle. After washing it, he could read the words "Guinness Extra Stout, London" on the seal. Up to 20 bottles were found in total. Sand had probably covered the cargo, which also included pickled vegetables, so the bottles had remained hidden for many years. In the cargo hold, the bottles were kept at about 4 degrees Celsius, under high pressure and in complete darkness, which helped to preserve them.

Samples of the beer have been sent to scientists at KU Leuven, a university in Belgium. According to Panis, there is a possibility that the beer is still drinkable, as long as seawater has not entered the bottles through the corks.

Panis and Paweł Truszynski, a diver and historical researcher, have also launched a project called "Project Jurassic Beer." They want to recreate the stout so that it tastes the way it would have in 1864. They are working with Kevin Verstrepen, a professor of microbiology at KU Leuven. Verstrepen said it is unlikely that living yeast can be recovered from the bottles. If not, he plans to study the yeast's DNA and use a modern relative instead. Truszynski said that success would be like a form of "liquid time travel."
The divers have also contacted Guinness. According to its parent company, Diageo, the Guinness Archive team has been talking with the divers to assess the discovery.
